title: Thornvale Country Market
transcript:
Speaker 1: Charlie: Hello. Thorn Vale Country Market. Charlie speaking.
Speaker 2: Julia: Hi. I’m calling because I’d like to open a couple of stalls to sell some of our products at your market.
Speaker 1: Charlie: Okay. I’ll have to get your details so I can fill out an application form. What’s your name?
Speaker 2: Julia: It’s Julia Smith.
Speaker 1: Charlie: I’ll just write that down. We also need a business name.
Speaker 2: Julia: It’s Sunrise Farm. You may not have heard of us. We recently changed our name from Sunrise Estate.
Speaker 1: Charlie: Is your property in the local area?
Speaker 2: Julia: It’s about 20 kilometres from here.
Speaker 1: Charlie: That’s great. We like to focus on local producers. Can I also get a contact phone number?
Speaker 2: Julia: My number’s 0407551827.
Speaker 1: Charlie: Got it. Is that your mobile number?
Speaker 2: Julia: That’s right.
Speaker 1: Charlie: And, Julia, can you also give me your address?
Speaker 2: Julia: Okay. It’s 789 Green Road, and that’s in Maplewood.
Speaker 1: Charlie: So shall we talk about your first stall? What are you planning to sell?
Speaker 2: Julia: I’ve been to your market, and I know you’ve got a lot of vegetable stalls, but we want to sell flowers. We’ll pick them every morning before we come to the market. We’ve been growing them for about a year. We grow fruit too, but it’s just for ourselves at the moment.
Speaker 1: Charlie: Okay. I’m sure you’ll get plenty of customers.
Speaker 2: Julia: We hope so.
Speaker 1: Charlie: Are you planning to sell anything else at the stall?
Speaker 2: Julia: Well, my husband is a talented carpenter in his spare time. I’ve convinced him to turn his hobby into a small business.
Speaker 1: Charlie: What does he make? The market attracts a lot of customers looking for unique handicrafts made by local artists and craftsmen.
Speaker 2: Julia: He makes some lovely furniture. It’s all made out of locally sourced wood.
Speaker 1: Charlie: I see. We have other craftsmen at our market selling things like glass products and ceramic goods, so you’ll fit in.
Speaker 2: Julia: Great. Do we get a choice as to where we will be located?
Speaker 1: Charlie: Certainly. Our market’s very big. There’s what’s known as the town end, and the opposite end is known as the river end.
Speaker 2: Julia: That sounds better. That’s where we’d like to be. If we’re spending all day there, we may as well have some lovely scenery to look at. Now I want to ask you about the size of the stall. What size is your standard space?
Speaker 1: Charlie: Our standard sites are 3.6 metres at the front and a length of 5.4 metres.
Speaker 2: Julia: We might need a bit more space than that.
Speaker 1: Charlie: In that case, you can book a larger site with a length of 7.5 metres.
Speaker 2: Julia: We’ll do that.
Speaker 1: Charlie: So what about your second stall?
Speaker 2: Julia: Well, we own a small café in town, and we’d like to try opening a stall at the market.
Speaker 1: Charlie: What would you like to sell? Coffee, I suppose?
Speaker 2: Julia: Well, we specialise in tea, actually. It’s all organic too. We’re pretty famous for that locally.
Speaker 1: Charlie: If you’re serving anything to eat or drink, you’ll need a food licence, obviously. That’s a must at our market.
Speaker 2: Julia: That’s fine. We’ve got that.
Speaker 1: Charlie: Is there anything else you want to sell? Cakes? Sandwiches?
Speaker 2: Julia: Well, we’ve recently started making our own chocolate, so we’d like to bring a few different kinds along to see how they go.
Speaker 1: Charlie: Great. Where would you like this stall to be located?
Speaker 2: Julia: Well, with this one, we really want to be close to the entrance. That way we’ll get the highest number of potential customers walking past.
Speaker 1: Charlie: That’s a very sought-after location, but I’m sure we can find you a spot. And do you have any special requirements at all?
Speaker 2: Julia: We’ll have some equipment that needs to be powered, so we’ll need a site that has electricity. We’ll set up our own chairs as well. Is that okay?
Speaker 1: Charlie: Sure. And now we just need to talk …
